questions.question: You are travelling in the metro and sitting on a seat reserved for senior citizens. At the next station, a young woman around 29 years old boards the train. She appears attractive, well-dressed and confident. As soon as she comes near you, she asks you to vacate the seat immediately, even though the seat is not reserved for women but specifically for senior citizens. In such a situation, what will you do?
questions.questionHtml:
You are travelling in the metro and sitting on a seat reserved for senior citizens. At the next station, a young woman around 29 years old boards the train. She appears attractive, well-dressed and confident. As soon as she comes near you, she asks you to vacate the seat immediately, even though the seat is not reserved for women but specifically for senior citizens.

In such a situation, what will you do?

options.text: Get defensive and argue loudly, escalating the situation.
options.html: Get defensive and argue loudly, escalating the situation.

options.text: Get up immediately and offer her the seat, thinking it is better to avoid any argument.
options.html: Get up immediately and offer her the seat, thinking it is better to avoid any argument.

options.text: Politely explain that the seat is reserved for senior citizens, not women, and offer to help her find another seat.
options.html: Politely explain that the seat is reserved for senior citizens, not women, and offer to help her find another seat.

options.text: Ask the nearby commuters or metro staff to intervene and clarify the rule about reserved seats.
options.html: Ask the nearby commuters or metro staff to intervene and clarify the rule about reserved seats.

questions.solution:
The correct option is A: Politely explain that the seat is reserved for senior citizens, not women, and offer to help her find another seat.

Explanation: This response is respectful and clear. You are not being rude or confrontational. You are simply stating the rule about the seat and showing kindness by offering help. It avoids unnecessary conflict and keeps the situation calm.

questions.question: Ajay ranked sixteenth from the top and twenty-ninth from the bottom among those who passed an examination. Six boys did not participate in the competition and five failed in it. How many boys were there in the class?
questions.questionHtml: Ajay ranked sixteenth from the top and twenty-ninth from the bottom among those who passed an examination. Six boys did not participate in the competition and five failed in it. How many boys were there in the class?
questions.solution:
Formula:
Rank from top + Rank from bottom – 1 = Total who passed

= 16 + 29 – 1
= 44 boys passed.

Step 2: Add boys who failed and did not participate

Total boys in class = Passed + Failed + Not participated
= 44 + 5 + 6
= 55

questions.question: Study the following information carefully to answer the questions given below: A reputed educational foundation is to select meritorious graduate students for the award of scholarships for higher studies abroad who fulfil the following criteria: (i) Age — More than 20 years but less than 25 years, as on 1.4.2007. (ii) Minimum percentage of marks — B.Sc. 60% or B.A. 50% or B.Com. 55%. (iii) Prizes/Awards — Should have won at least one either in Essay, Debate or Sports. (iv) Annual family income — Not to be more than ₹1,00,000. (v) Domicile — Must be staying in India for the last 15 years or above, as on 1.4.2007. Concessions: One has to fulfil the above conditions. However, certain concessions are available to the following categories: (A) Wards of farmers (F) — Relaxation in the maximum age limit up to five years. (B) SC/ST applicants (S) — Relaxation in percentage of marks up to 5%. Consideration: (C) Not fulfilling criterion (iii) above — the case may be referred to the Secretary of the Foundation. (D) Not fulfilling criterion (iv) above — the case may be referred to Chairman of the Foundation. You have to study the information provided for a candidate and decide the course of action. Kewal, who will be 23 years old on 1.1.2009, passed B.Com. with 52% marks. His father, a Government employee, has been working at Srinagar since 1989 whose present monthly salary is ₹8200. Kewal got the 3rd prize in the State Essay Competition.
